Build an Affiliate Program Without Paying for Coupon Leaks

Playbooklowob research

By lowob · 25 May 2026 · 7-minute read · Distribution

Affiliate programmes can introduce new customers, but weak commission rules also reward partners for sales that would have happened anyway. The most common leak is a coupon site or browser extension that appears at checkout, after the customer has decided, and collects the commission under last-click attribution. Google judged the practice serious enough to change its Chrome Web Store rules in 2025. The fix is in the terms: what is paid for, who qualifies, what is prohibited and how outcomes are validated, set before the programme goes on a network.

An affiliate programme is a set of terms under which other people are paid to bring you customers.

That is all it is, and it is why the channel is so often misjudged. Companies picture coupon sites and conclude the channel is low quality. Or they picture a network dashboard and assume the programme runs itself. Both are true of badly built programmes. Neither is true of a programme that was designed.

For a company in a category the ad platforms restrict, the affiliate channel has a property few others have: no platform has to approve each placement. Partners choose to carry the product because the terms make it worth their while. That does not remove the rules on what partners say, which the last section covers.

The coupon leak

Start with the failure, because most companies are living in it.

A customer decides to buy. At checkout, they search for a discount code. A coupon site appears, offers a code and drops a cookie. Under last-click attribution, that site is paid a commission for a customer who had already decided.

Multiply by every checkout and the programme is paying a tax on its own conversions. The reported numbers look excellent, because the programme appears to drive sales that were happening anyway. The finance team sees a rising affiliate bill and a flat top line and concludes, correctly, that something is wrong. Our piece on attribution vs incrementality explains why the reported number and the caused number diverge.

Browser extensions are the automated version of the same leak. In March 2025 Google tightened its Chrome Web Store policy so that an extension may add or replace affiliate links only when the programme is disclosed, the user takes an action first, and the link "is tied to a direct benefit for the user at that moment." A coupon extension "must not insert an affiliate link if no coupon or discount is found." Enforcement began on 10 June 2025, with removal from the store for violations. A platform rule is not a fix for your programme, but it confirms the leak is real.

The industry is aware of it. At a September 2025 Performance Marketing Association session on coupons, practitioners said "most programs are still last click", that public vanity codes "can be scraped", and recommended single-use or capped codes and commissioning "for contribution rather than proximity to checkout."

The fix is in the terms, not the platform. Exclude or tier coupon and loyalty partners. Pay on first click, or on a weighted model, for content partners who introduced the customer. Require that a discount code be one the partner was issued, not one scraped from the checkout page. Approve partners individually rather than accepting every application.

Design the terms before choosing the network

A programme's terms determine who joins it. Set them first.

TermDecisionDefault to avoid
What is paid forA funded account, an approved application, a first transaction above a threshold, a subscriber retained at 30 daysPaying on the event that is easiest to count
How much, for how longFlat bounty, percentage or revenue share, with a cookie window that matches the buying cycleOne window for every product
Who qualifiesContent publishers, comparison sites, creators, communities, coupon and loyalty sites, sub-networks, each on stated termsAccepting every application
What is prohibitedBrand-name bidding, misleading claims, unissued codes, incentivised traffic, unapproved regulated claimsRelying on the network's standard list
How outcomes are validatedWhich events your own tracking confirms, validation period, treatment of refunds, chargebacks and fraudPaying on the network's report alone

Cookie windows should reflect the real decision: seven days for a decision people make in an afternoon, sixty for one they research. Prohibitions for regulated products should include any language the company could not say itself.

Only then choose where the programme lives. The large networks bring existing partners and handle payments; some carry restricted categories and some do not, which is the first thing to check. A direct platform gives more control and less reach. A company can run both.

Whoever runs it, keep judgment in-house. Edelman and Brandi's study in the Journal of Marketing Research, of merchants overseeing thousands of affiliates they had never met, found outside specialists were better at excluding affiliates that clearly broke the rules, while in-house staff were better at catching "borderline" affiliates whose practices still worked against the merchant. Coupon leakage is usually borderline, not fraud.

The fix for the coupon leak is in the terms, not the platform.

Recruit like a partner programme, not a listing

A programme on a network with no recruitment is a listing. Partners do not find it; they are found.

Choose the first thirty partners by hand: the comparison sites that already rank for the category, the newsletters whose readers already ask about it, the creators whose audience already buys similar products, and the communities where the question already comes up. Each gets a specific offer, product access, creative that does not need to be rebuilt, and a named person to talk to.

That is a few weeks of work. It is also why the channel keeps producing when the platforms change their minds about the category. The market is large enough to reward it: the Performance Marketing Association's 2025 study put US affiliate investment at about $13.6 billion in 2024, with financial services rising from 12% to 15% of spend. Our Partner channel design covers how to set roles and tiers once the base grows.

What a programme that works looks like

Signallowob's working thresholdWhy it matters
Approved outcomesRising month over monthThe only volume that counts
Coupon partners' share of paid outcomesBelow a fifthAbove it, much of the bill is likely the leak
Largest single partnerBelow a third of paid outcomesConcentration is a dependency
Approval rateAbove 90%Low rates mean poor traffic or poor terms
Cost per approved outcomeStable or falling as the mix improvesShows the partner base is getting better
Partner behaviourAsking for creative before you send itPartners invested in the product

The thresholds are lowob's working rules, not industry standards. For context, the PMA reported that coupon sites' share of US affiliate investment fell from 16% to 10%, while loyalty and cashback held at 35%. If loyalty partners also sit at checkout in your programme, count them with the coupon share.

That is an asset. It has terms, a partner base, a reporting history and a reason to keep working when any single channel goes dark. Unlike a rented ad account, it is something the company owns.

Disclosure and responsibility

Where affiliates endorse products or receive commissions, disclosure matters too. The US FTC's endorsement guidance says affiliates should disclose the relationship clearly, close to the recommendation, and that "affiliate link" on its own is not enough. It also says advertisers "need to have reasonable programs in place to train and monitor members of their network", and that delegating to an outside company "doesn't relieve you of responsibility." For regulated financial products in the UK, the FCA's FG24/1 guidance says firms working with affiliates should take proactive responsibility for their promotions. Other jurisdictions impose different rules, so write the disclosure language into the terms and check it.

lowob takeaways

  • Define the action worth paying for before recruiting affiliates. Pay for the event that matters, validated by your own tracking.
  • Close the coupon leak in the terms. Tier coupon and loyalty partners, issue single-use codes and pay content partners for introductions.
  • Check whether partners introduce customers you would not otherwise reach. Recruit the first thirty by hand.
  • Choose partners whose audiences have a genuine need for the product. Approve individually and keep borderline calls in-house.
  • Own the disclosure. The advertiser stays responsible for what affiliates say.

Common questions

How do coupon sites affect affiliate programmes?

Under last-click attribution, a coupon site that appears at checkout can be paid a commission for a customer who had already decided to buy. Tier or exclude coupon partners, issue single-use codes and pay content partners who introduced the customer.

What is a good affiliate commission structure?

Pay for a validated event that matters, such as an approved application or a retained subscriber, with a cookie window that matches the buying cycle and clear rules for refunds, chargebacks and fraud.

Are browser coupon extensions allowed to replace affiliate links?

Under Chrome Web Store policy enforced from June 2025, extensions may apply affiliate links only after a user action, with disclosure, and when the user gets a direct benefit such as a coupon actually found.

Do affiliates have to disclose commissions?

In the US, the FTC says affiliates should clearly disclose that they are paid, close to the recommendation, and that advertisers must train and monitor their affiliates.

Sources and notes

  • Google, Chrome Web Store policy updates: strengthening our policies on affiliate programs in Chrome extensions, 11 March 2025. Platform policy announcement; enforcement from 10 June 2025.
  • Performance Marketing Association, Beyond the Affiliate Coupon Code, webinar held 23 September 2025. Trade body summary of a practitioner panel; qualitative, with figures from the PMA study.
  • Performance Marketing Association, Industry Study 2025, 18 June 2025. Trade association research with London Research; methodology not stated in the release.
  • Edelman and Brandi, Risk, Information, and Incentives in Online Affiliate Marketing, Journal of Marketing Research 52(1), 2015. Academic study; data predates current extension rules.
  • FTC, Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking, last updated July 2025. US staff guidance, not a rule.
  • FCA, FG24/1 Finalised guidance on financial promotions on social media, 26 March 2024. UK guidance for regulated financial promotions.

Export last quarter's affiliate payouts and tag each partner as content, comparison, creator, community, coupon or loyalty. If coupon and loyalty partners take more than a fifth of paid outcomes, rewrite their terms before the next payout cycle.
